candidates.theme_relation: Dominant AI data-center compute supplier; maps hyperscaler and AI-cloud capex into GPUs, systems, NVLink, InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet and software-stack demand.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Custom AI ASICs / AI networking semiconductors
candidates.theme_relation: Key supplier for hyperscaler custom AI accelerators and high-speed networking silicon; relevant to both GPU substitution and AI cluster fabric scaling.
High-confidence AI chokepoint because AI accelerator output depends on HBM bandwidth, stacking, qualification, yield and limited leading-edge memory capacity.
Critical AI supply-chain node for leading-edge accelerator wafers and CoWoS-like GPU/HBM integration capacity.
Core AI demand owner; converts enterprise AI adoption into cloud AI revenue and demand for GPUs, custom accelerators, networking, data centers, power and software.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Data-center power, thermal and critical digital infrastructure
candidates.theme_relation: Physical-infrastructure bottleneck supplier; high-density AI racks require power delivery, cooling and reliability before chips can generate revenue.
AI cluster scaling requires high-speed, reliable, low-latency networking; Arista maps to Ethernet-based AI fabrics and cloud-scale data-center switching.
Potential beneficiary if hyperscalers diversify accelerator supply, optimize inference cost, or seek open software alternatives around ROCm and MI-series accelerators.
AWS capex and AI-chip strategy shape demand for external GPUs, custom silicon, networking, data-center infrastructure and AI cloud services.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Cloud hyperscaler / consumer internet AI / custom silicon
candidates.theme_relation: Full-stack AI platform with internal and external AI demand; TPU adoption is a key test of custom-silicon substitution versus merchant GPU dependence.
Large non-cloud AI infrastructure buyer; demand affects GPUs, servers, networking, memory, data centers and power, while monetization tests AI capex ROI.
Alternative AI cloud capacity provider; RPO conversion is a public signal for contracted AI compute demand outside the largest hyperscalers.
Pure-play gauge of AI compute demand, GPU availability, customer concentration, data-center execution and debt-funded capex risk.
Benefits if the AI bottleneck shifts from chips to power delivery, switchgear, electrical distribution, grid interconnection and equipment lead times.
Converts accelerators into deployable servers and racks; backlog and margins help test whether chip demand becomes installed AI compute capacity.

candidates.sector_or_industry: AI servers / rack-scale systems / liquid cooling
candidates.theme_relation: High-beta AI data-center systems integrator where speed, GPU platform support and liquid-cooling capability matter, but accounting and execution risk require validation.
Structural upstream chokepoint for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing capacity used by AI accelerators and advanced logic.
US-listed memory supplier exposed to AI HBM, server DRAM and enterprise storage demand; relevance depends on HBM qualification, capacity ramp and pricing cycle.
Potentially important AI memory and foundry supplier; priority depends on HBM competitiveness, customer qualification and foundry share in AI accelerators.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Custom silicon / optical DSP / data-center semiconductors
candidates.theme_relation: Maps to custom compute and high-speed data-center connectivity; useful for AI networking and ASIC diversification checks.
AI clusters increase demand for high-speed optical interconnect, transceivers and photonics components; candidate for networking bottleneck research.
Potential beneficiary of AI data-center optical links, lasers and photonics demand as cluster scale pushes bandwidth and reach requirements.
AI training and inference growth can increase demand for data-center interconnect, metro optical capacity and high-bandwidth network systems.
Cloud hardware manufacturing and networking systems exposure; useful breadth candidate beyond mega-cap semiconductor names.
AI rack and networking density can increase need for high-speed connectors, cable assemblies and interconnect components.
Potential second-order beneficiary from dense AI data-center interconnect, power connectivity and broader electrification infrastructure.
Maps AI compute demand into real estate, power availability, leasing backlog and connected metro data-center capacity.
Enterprise and cloud AI workloads may increase demand for interconnected colocation capacity, though hyperscale AI training may be less directly exposed than power-dense wholesale sites.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Electrical equipment / data-center power and energy management
candidates.theme_relation: International public-market mapping for AI data-center electrical distribution, energy management, automation and thermal infrastructure.
Relevant if AI infrastructure bottlenecks shift to electrification, power distribution, automation and grid-side equipment.
AI data-center growth may increase demand for grid equipment, transmission infrastructure and power-system upgrades.
Potential beneficiary of AI-driven load growth through power generation, grid modernization and energy infrastructure demand.
AI data-center load growth increases strategic value of reliable clean power and long-term power purchase agreements.
AI load growth may support demand for dispatchable power and electricity supply in constrained data-center markets.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing construction services
candidates.theme_relation: Potential beneficiary of AI data-center construction where mechanical, electrical and cooling execution capacity becomes a deployment bottleneck.
AI data-center buildouts require electrical and mechanical construction capacity; backlog and data-center mix should be validated.
Enterprise AI depends on governed, usable data; Snowflake maps to data infrastructure and AI application enablement rather than physical chokepoints.
AI workloads can raise monitoring, observability and infrastructure-management complexity; revenue linkage requires later evidence validation.
AI applications require operational data layers; MongoDB is a second-order software infrastructure candidate needing validation of AI-driven demand.
Tests whether AI monetization reaches enterprise application workflows through agentic products rather than remaining concentrated in infrastructure.
Enterprise AI automation candidate; validates whether AI agents reduce manual workflows and support software monetization.
Agentic automation exposure; relevant to downstream AI productivity adoption but needs proof of durable revenue acceleration and competitive positioning.

candidates.sector_or_industry: AI software / data platforms / government and enterprise analytics
candidates.theme_relation: Maps to enterprise and government AI deployment at the software layer; requires later market-pricing and revenue-quality checks.
Generative AI monetization candidate at the application layer; less direct chokepoint exposure than infrastructure suppliers.
AI custom silicon and data-center CPU design may increase relevance of Arm IP; direct chokepoint strength requires license and royalty evidence.
Upstream equipment supplier for logic, memory and packaging capacity expansion tied to AI semiconductor demand.
Relevant upstream supplier for memory and logic manufacturing intensity, including AI-driven HBM and advanced process capacity.
AI chip and advanced packaging ramps increase importance of yield control, inspection and metrology at leading-edge nodes.
AI accelerators and HBM increase testing complexity and capital intensity; direct international mapping for semiconductor test chokepoints.
International upstream equipment supplier exposed to leading-edge logic and memory capacity required for AI semiconductor supply.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Semiconductor dicing, grinding and polishing equipment
candidates.theme_relation: HBM stacking and advanced packaging can increase demand for wafer thinning, dicing and precision processing equipment.
OSAT exposure to advanced packaging and test; relevance depends on share in AI accelerator packaging/test flows versus TSMC-integrated capacity.
US-listed OSAT candidate for advanced packaging and test capacity; AI relevance needs customer and package-type validation.
Advanced AI accelerators require high-end substrates; substrate capacity and qualification may act as a packaging-adjacent bottleneck.
AI accelerators and servers increase demand for advanced substrates and high-performance boards; direct exposure requires customer/program validation.

coverage_gaps: AI networking and optical interconnect still need a dedicated split by Ethernet switches, InfiniBand, retimers, DSPs, linear-drive optics, CPO, transceivers, fiber and network operating software.
Storage and data pipelines remain under-covered: eSSD, nearline HDD, vector databases, data governance, ETL, observability, backup and AI security infrastructure should receive deeper Layer 2 work.

International public-market coverage is only partially represented; more validation is needed for SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, TSMC, ASML, Advantest, Tokyo Electron, Disco, Ibiden, Unimicron, ASE, Amkor, Schneider Electric, ABB and Siemens Energy.

Private AI demand owners and infrastructure firms are not directly investable but should be tracked as demand signals: OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, CoreWeave-like cloud providers, Crusoe-like energy/AI infrastructure firms, and private cooling/optical startups.

Regulatory and geopolitical risks need a separate layer: export controls, China accelerator restrictions, nuclear permitting, grid interconnection rules, data-center moratoria, water restrictions and power-cost pass-through.
Market-pricing checks are deferred; this universe ranks Serenity research relevance only and does not assess valuation, expected returns or suitability for any trade.

memory_update.text: AI should be tracked as an infrastructure-to-software system: hyperscaler and AI-cloud capex pulls semiconductors, HBM, packaging, networking, power/cooling, grid, data infrastructure and enterprise automation software.
Highest-confidence Layer 1 AI chokepoints are accelerated compute, HBM, advanced packaging, AI networking/optical interconnect, and data-center power/cooling.
Advanced packaging, especially CoWoS-like GPU/HBM integration capacity, should remain distinct from leading-edge wafer fabrication in later scoring.

Power availability, grid interconnection, liquid cooling and electrical balance-of-plant are becoming first-order constraints for AI data-center deployment rather than generic infrastructure afterthoughts.
The universe still needs deeper node-level evidence for optical interconnect, storage, data pipelines, AI security, international semicap equipment, substrates and grid equipment.
Private AI model builders and AI infrastructure providers should be tracked as non-public demand signals even when they cannot appear as direct public-market candidates.

summary: Merged Layer 1 AI universe across demand owners, accelerators, custom ASICs, HBM/memory, foundry, advanced packaging, networking/optical interconnect, AI servers, power/cooling, data-center real estate, grid/electrical equipment, and enterprise AI software. Ranking is Serenity relevance for further research, not a buy/sell view. Highest-priority nodes are those closest to hard-to-bypass chokepoints: accelerated compute, HBM, advanced packaging, AI networking, power/cooling, and contracted AI cloud demand.
